problem_text: A wave has a frequency of 500 Hz and a wavelength of 0.68 m. What is the wave speed?

hints.text: What is the fundamental wave equation?
v = fλ
Multiply frequency by wavelength.

solution_explanation: Wave speed v = fλ = (500 Hz)(0.68 m) = 340 m/s.

problem_text: A guitar string 0.65 m long vibrates in its fundamental mode at 440 Hz. What is the speed of waves on the string?

pattern_refs.application_notes: Fundamental mode of string fixed at both ends

hints.text: For a string fixed at both ends, what is the wavelength of the fundamental?
Fundamental: L = λ/2, so λ = 2L
Then use v = fλ.

solution_explanation: For fundamental mode: λ = 2L = 2(0.65) = 1.30 m. Wave speed v = fλ = (440)(1.30) = 572 m/s.

problem_text: A closed pipe (closed at one end) is 0.5 m long. What is the frequency of its fundamental mode? (Speed of sound = 340 m/s)

hints.text: For a closed pipe, what is at the closed end and what is at the open end?
Node at closed end, antinode at open end. Fundamental: L = λ/4.
So λ = 4L, then f = v/λ.

solution_explanation: For closed pipe fundamental: L = λ/4, so λ = 4L = 4(0.5) = 2 m. Frequency f = v/λ = 340/2 = 170 Hz.

problem_text: An ambulance with a siren at 1000 Hz approaches you at 30 m/s. What frequency do you hear? (Speed of sound = 340 m/s)

hints.text: What is the Doppler effect formula?
f' = f(v ± v_o)/(v ∓ v_s). Source approaching = denominator smaller.
f' = f × v/(v - v_s) when source approaches stationary observer.

problem_text: Light travels from air (n = 1.00) into water (n = 1.33) at an angle of incidence of 45°. What is the angle of refraction?

hints.text: What is Snell's law?
n₁sin(θ₁) = n₂sin(θ₂)
Solve for θ₂: sin(θ₂) = n₁sin(θ₁)/n₂

problem_text: What is the critical angle for light traveling from glass (n = 1.5) to air (n = 1.0)?

hints.text: What is the formula for critical angle?
sin(θ_c) = n₂/n₁ where n₁ > n₂
Critical angle exists only when going from higher to lower n.

solution_explanation: Critical angle: sin(θ_c) = n₂/n₁ = 1.0/1.5 = 0.667. θ_c = arcsin(0.667) = 41.8°.

problem_text: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror with focal length 20 cm. Where is the image located?

hints.text: What is the mirror equation?
Solve for d_i: 1/d_i = 1/f - 1/d_o

solution_explanation: Mirror equation: 1/f = 1/d_o + 1/d_i. 1/d_i = 1/20 - 1/30 = 3/60 - 2/60 = 1/60. So d_i = 60 cm (real image).

problem_text: A converging lens has a focal length of 15 cm. An object is placed 10 cm from the lens. Where is the image and what is the magnification?

hints.text: Use the thin lens equation: 1/f = 1/d_o + 1/d_i
Solve for d_i, then calculate m = -d_i/d_o
A negative d_i means virtual image on same side as object.

solution_explanation: 1/d_i = 1/f - 1/d_o = 1/15 - 1/10 = 2/30 - 3/30 = -1/30. So d_i = -30 cm (virtual image). Magnification m = -d_i/d_o = -(-30)/10 = +3 (upright, magnified).

problem_text: In a double-slit experiment, the slits are 0.2 mm apart and the screen is 1.5 m away. If light of wavelength 600 nm is used, what is the distance between adjacent bright fringes?

hints.text: What is the formula for fringe spacing in double-slit interference?
Δy = λL/d
Convert units: 600 nm = 600 × 10⁻⁹ m, 0.2 mm = 0.2 × 10⁻³ m

problem_text: Light of wavelength 500 nm passes through a single slit of width 0.1 mm. At what angle is the first diffraction minimum?

hints.text: What is the condition for minima in single-slit diffraction?
a sin(θ) = mλ for minima (m = 1, 2, 3, ...)
For first minimum, m = 1.

solution_explanation: First minimum: a sin(θ) = λ. sin(θ) = λ/a = (500 × 10⁻⁹)/(0.1 × 10⁻³) = 5 × 10⁻³. θ = arcsin(0.005) = 0.29°.

problem_text: Unpolarized light of intensity I₀ passes through two polarizers. The first is vertical; the second is at 30° to vertical. What is the final intensity?

hints.text: What happens when unpolarized light passes through the first polarizer?
First polarizer: I₁ = I₀/2
Second polarizer (Malus's law): I₂ = I₁cos²(θ)

rubric: First polarizer gives I₀/2, then multiply by cos²(30°) = 3/4

solution_explanation: After first polarizer: I₁ = I₀/2. After second (Malus's law): I₂ = I₁cos²(30°) = (I₀/2)(√3/2)² = (I₀/2)(3/4) = 3I₀/8 = 0.375I₀.

problem_text: A soap film (n = 1.33) in air appears bright green (λ = 540 nm) when viewed at normal incidence. What is the minimum thickness of the film?

hints.text: Consider phase changes on reflection.
Top surface (air to film): phase change. Bottom (film to air): no phase change.
With one phase change, constructive: 2nt = (m + ½)λ. Minimum t is for m = 0.

solution_explanation: One phase change (at top surface). Constructive interference: 2nt = (m + ½)λ. For minimum thickness, m = 0: 2nt = λ/2. t = λ/(4n) = 540/(4 × 1.33) = 101.5 nm.

problem_text: Two waves with the same frequency and amplitude travel in opposite directions on a string. At a point where they meet, the amplitudes are both 5 cm. What are the maximum and minimum displacements at that point?

hints.text: What is the superposition principle?
Maximum occurs when waves are in phase (constructive).
Minimum occurs when waves are out of phase (destructive).

solution_explanation: Constructive (in phase): A_max = 5 + 5 = 10 cm. Destructive (out of phase): A_min = |5 - 5| = 0 cm.

problem_text: A sound has an intensity of 10⁻⁶ W/m². What is its intensity level in decibels? (I₀ = 10⁻¹² W/m²)

hints.text: What is the formula for decibel level?
β = 10 log(I/I₀)
Calculate log(10⁻⁶/10⁻¹²) = log(10⁶) = 6

problem_text: What is Brewster's angle for light reflecting from glass (n = 1.5) in air?

hints.text: What is the formula for Brewster's angle?
tan(θ_B) = n₂/n₁
For light in air hitting glass: tan(θ_B) = n_glass/n_air = 1.5/1

solution_explanation: Brewster's angle: tan(θ_B) = n₂/n₁ = 1.5/1.0 = 1.5. θ_B = arctan(1.5) = 56.3°.

problem_text: A convex mirror has a focal length of -20 cm. An object is placed 30 cm from the mirror. Where is the image and is it real or virtual?

hints.text: Use the mirror equation with f negative for convex mirror.
Negative d_i means virtual image.

solution_explanation: 1/d_i = 1/f - 1/d_o = 1/(-20) - 1/30 = -3/60 - 2/60 = -5/60 = -1/12. So d_i = -12 cm. Virtual image (negative), behind the mirror.

problem_text: An open pipe is 1.0 m long. What are the frequencies of the first three harmonics? (Speed of sound = 340 m/s)

hints.text: For an open pipe, what are the boundary conditions?
Antinodes at both ends. All harmonics present: f_n = nv/(2L).
n = 1, 2, 3 for first three harmonics.

solution_explanation: Open pipe: f_n = nv/(2L) = n(340)/(2×1) = 170n Hz. f₁ = 170 Hz, f₂ = 340 Hz, f₃ = 510 Hz.

problem_text: In a double-slit experiment, what happens to the fringe spacing if the wavelength is doubled?

pattern_refs.application_notes: Effect of wavelength on fringe pattern

hints.text: What is the formula for fringe spacing?
Δy = λL/d
How does Δy depend on λ?

solution_explanation: Fringe spacing Δy = λL/d is directly proportional to wavelength. If λ doubles, Δy doubles.

problem_text: A diverging lens has a focal length of -10 cm. An object is placed 15 cm from the lens. What is the magnification?

hints.text: First find d_i using the lens equation.
Then m = -d_i/d_o

problem_text: Two speakers emit sound waves of frequency 680 Hz in phase. A listener stands at a point where the path difference from the two speakers is 0.75 m. Is the interference constructive or destructive? (Speed of sound = 340 m/s)

hints.text: First find the wavelength.
Express path difference in terms of wavelength.
Constructive if path diff = nλ, destructive if path diff = (n+½)λ.

solution_explanation: λ = v/f = 340/680 = 0.5 m. Path difference = 0.75 m = 1.5λ = (1 + ½)λ. This is (n + ½)λ with n = 1, so destructive interference.
